newsitem.title: CHINA: HK unionist on hunger strike, blasts tycoon-rule.
newsitem.headline: HK unionist on hunger strike, blasts tycoon-rule.

text.p: A Hong Kong unionist launched a hunger strike on Wednesday to protest at the government's plan to suspend newly passed labour laws, calling the administration a tool of business tycoons uninterested in workers' rights.

"It is not really Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong," Lee Cheuk-yan told Reuters, citing Beijing's promise of autonomy following the territory's reversion to China . "It is Hong Kong tycoons ruling Hong Kong."

Lee, secretary general of the Hong Kong Confederation of Trade Unions, said he would consume only liquids for five days in protest, and lead a march to Hong Kong Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa's office on Sunday.
The confederation also said in a statement that the administration's move to suspend the ordinances was a backward step for labour rights, democracy and the rule of law.

Tung's government asked Hong Kong's provisional legislature on Tuesday to rush through a bill suspending seven laws passed by the pre-handover legislature in the final days of British rule -- including labour laws moved by then-legislator Lee.

Lee lost his seat on July 1, when the elected legislature was scrapped half-way through its four-year term following the British colony's handover to China and replaced by a council chosen by a Beijing-backed committee.
The ordinances provide protection against anti-union discrimination by employers and allow collective bargaining by unions on their members' behalf.
Business interests were outraged, saying the laws had to be abolished before they undermined investors' confidence in Hong Kong and ruined harmonious employer-employee relationships.
